visual_anchors.morphology_description: Upper pharmaceutical column-vessel. Tall multi-segmented cylindrical apothecary column with 3–4 barrel-shaped chambers stacked vertically, separated by narrow ringed bands. A flat disc-shaped lid caps the top. The barrel sections are painted with BLUE-GREY wash — this blue fill is the primary STATE-OF-MATTER indicator: the blue pigment, applied as a wash within the barrel chambers, strongly suggests a LIQUID content. The fill is uneven and painterly (not geometric), resembling a fluid level. No visible horizontal 'liquid surface line' but the blue wash occupies the lower-to-mid sections of each barrel, consistent with partial-fill liquid state. The segmented structure may represent a multi-stage distillation column or stacked storage unit for a liquid preparation. Small dot ornaments or circles along the sides of some segments may represent rivets, measurement marks, or decorative bands.
